what: Why the dated-basket historical Hawkes replay produces no fits, measured. The binding constraint is point-in-time basket coverage, not the refit cadence and not execution cost.
supersedes: An earlier reading in this session that extrapolated 'hours per fit' from 35 minutes of wall time with zero completed fits. That extrapolation was wrong in both directions and is replaced by the per-candidate measurements below.

measured_cost_on_the_real_path.note: A first timing attempt used the live config basket, whose rebalance_date (2026-07-01) postdates every historical cutoff, so fit_pending short-circuited with `no_eligible_basket` after reading 0 rows in 0.5s. That measured nothing. These samples resolve the epoch's own basket first, which is what `--baskets dated` does.
measured_cost_on_the_real_path.conclusion: The full replay is about five hours of compute, which is affordable. Cost was never the blocker.

two_mechanisms_confirmed_working.data_cutoff_separation: fit_pending reported observed_sessions=500 at a 2025-02-05 BAR cutoff even though every row in the native history carries a 2026 arrival. A raw NativeHistory.rows() call with a single cutoff returns 0 rows at that date, because it filters received_at <= mark with the same mark. That 0-versus-500 contrast is the original defect and its fix, observed side by side.
two_mechanisms_confirmed_working.arrival_discipline: At the 2026-10-23 candidate, rows() returned exactly 4,150,272 rows -- the original 2026-10-22 receipt batch, excluding the 1,593,993 rows received 2026-10-25. The re-seed did not backdate a single arrival.
two_mechanisms_confirmed_working.cadence_respected: The final candidate returned refit_not_due, which is correct: a compatible fit already exists at 2026-10-22 and the declared cadence is five sessions.

the_actual_blocker.finding: 70 distinct symbols appear in the dated epoch baskets and have NO intraday bars in the store at all. Every one of the 70 has since left the universe -- none is in today's 95-member basket. The depth backfill acquired today's members; a point-in-time basket needs the members that epoch actually had.
the_actual_blocker.why_incomplete_members_exceeds_the_missi: At 2025-02-05 the 500-session window reaches back past 2023-09-01 into the sparse era where only the ~17 deep-history members hold bars, so members present in the store are still incomplete ACROSS THAT WINDOW. 82 incomplete against 23 absent is that effect.
the_actual_blocker.consequence: Only the current epoch has complete coverage, and its candidates are refit_not_due. So the replay as it stands can produce zero historical fits -- not because of the cadence, and not because of cost.

remedy_executed.action: Acquire 5-minute intraday bars for the departed epoch-basket members over the same era today's members cover, 2023-09-01 to 2026-10-23.
remedy_executed.why_this_is_not_a_methodology_change: It changes no equation, threshold, window, cadence or basket rule. The point-in-time basket discipline REQUIRES data for the members each epoch actually had; without it the replay either fails, as it does now, or would have to substitute today's basket, which is look-ahead. Acquiring the data is what makes the declared method executable.
remedy_executed.broker_history_confirmed: Spot-checked ABB, ACC and ADANIENSOL: 450 candles each for the first week of 2023-09, i.e. 6 sessions x 75 bars. The depth exists.

residual_gaps.hfcl: The only member still without bars, in the 2024-07-01 and 2025-01-01 epochs. Deliberate: see one_symbol_blocked.
residual_gaps.2023_epochs: The 2023-01-01 and 2023-07-01 baskets have every member present but 71 and 72 of them hold their first bar on 2023-09-01, after the epoch date, because that is where this acquisition era begins. Candidates whose 500-session window reaches before 2023-09-01 therefore stay incomplete. Extending further back is more acquisition of the same kind, not a new problem.

one_symbol_blocked.finding: HFCL does not resolve against the broker's NSE EQ instrument list. It now trades as tradingsymbol `HFCL-BE`, instrument_token 5620225, name `HFCL` -- it has moved to the BE series (trade-for-trade settlement, a surveillance measure).
one_symbol_blocked.why_it_was_not_aliased: This is a SERIES change, not a rename, and the two are not interchangeable. A trade-for-trade counter has no intraday netting, so its microstructure and therefore its jump process differ from its EQ-series history. Splicing HFCL-BE bars onto HFCL's EQ-era basket membership would be a data-identity decision with scientific consequences. The repository's existing discipline for an identity change -- the TATAMOTORS/TMPV handling -- requires a dated exchange notice as evidence, and no such notice for this series move is held here.
one_symbol_blocked.blast_radius: HFCL appears in exactly two epoch baskets, 2024-07-01 and 2025-01-01. Those two epochs therefore stay short by one member. The 2025-07-01, 2026-01-01 and 2026-07-01 epochs do not contain it, and those are the epochs the candidates with a fully-covered window will use.
one_symbol_blocked.to_unblock: a dated NSE notice evidencing the series change, after which the alias can be registered the way the rename notice already is -- an owner-reviewable step, not an assumption.

what_this_does_not_change.readiness: Even with complete epoch coverage, a candidate set whose window lies entirely inside the all-member era yields roughly (779 - 500 + 1) = 280 candidates, about 56 fits at cadence 5. That is far short of 252, exactly as the cadence arithmetic already said. This work makes the replay produce real, verifiable historical vintages; it does not make the gate pass, and nothing here was tuned to make it pass.

seeding_integration_added.problem: scripts/prepare_native_hawkes.py seeded only the latest snapshot's basket, so the 69 newly acquired members would have landed in Postgres and never reached the native history the replay reads.
seeding_integration_added.change: Added --seed-members {config,dated-union}, default 'config' so every existing invocation is unchanged. 'dated-union' seeds the union of every snapshot's basket while the config keeps declaring the latest basket as `members`, because the live estimation path must not move when a replay needs deeper inputs. The config now records seed_policy and seeded_members so an artefact states which it was built with.
seeding_integration_added.testability: The selection was extracted into a pure seeded_symbols() helper and pinned by a regression test in tests/test_native_session_schedule.py covering: config returns the latest basket only, dated-union returns the union, the latest basket is always included, the result is deduplicated and ordered so a reseed is byte-stable, omitting the snapshots cannot silently widen anything, and an unknown policy raises.
seeding_integration_added.callers_checked: No programmatic callers exist; only docs and tests reference the script, and the default is unchanged.

fit_prediction_after_the_remedy.method: Read-only, from the history alone, before spending five hours: for each cadence candidate, does every member of ITS OWN epoch basket hold a bar on every date in the 500-session window? A proxy for the engine's completeness test, not a substitute -- the engine also applies the dated common-session policy, so its count can only be kinder.
fit_prediction_after_the_remedy.the_sharp_transition: 2025-08-08 has 71 incomplete members; 2025-09-16 has 0. Session 500 of the all-member era lands about 2025-09-05, so every earlier candidate's window reaches back before 2023-09-01 where only the deep-history members hold bars. 71 is the same count as the members whose first bar is 2023-09-01, which is the consistency check.
fit_prediction_after_the_remedy.conclusion: The remedy works: the replay moves from producing ZERO historical fits to about 56 real ones with point-in-time baskets and actual availability times. It still does not reach 252 at the declared cadence, which is the same conclusion the cadence arithmetic reached by a different route. Reaching 252 at cadence 5 would need 500 + 5x251 = 1,755 covered sessions, i.e. extending coverage for every epoch member back to roughly 2019.
